ownership_reason: Only the gold sees each backslash together with the character before it; hop 1 sees only whether the text holds a backslash at all, hop 2 owns the builder and hops 3 and 4 pass builder and text along. Once the gold has dropped an escaped backslash nothing in the result marks where it stood, and a change of the text before the gold cannot make the scan keep a backslash. The convention is pinned outside the gold: TokenQueue.chompBalanced takes the character directly after the escape character literally (`last != ESC`, with last the previous character) and tells callers to use unescape for its escaped output; QueryParser.contains and containsData unescape that output before matching text, while QueryParser.matches keeps the escapes for the regular expression; the facade's javadoc (a \ escaped string); TokenQueueTest chompEscapedBalanced and SelectorTest testPsuedoContainsWithParentheses and containsWithQuote pass (the escape character is dropped and the character it escapes is kept). The gold's javadoc promises the unescaped form of a backslash escaped text, which for `one \( \) \\` is `one ( ) \`. A one-line placeholder encoding at hop 1 (each doubled backslash replaced by U+0000 for the scan and turned back into a backslash afterwards) passes the existing tests but is not consistent with the path or the evidence: a text that holds U+0000 gets a backslash in its place, and a run of three backslashes before a character loses a second backslash, against chompBalanced's rule that the character after the escape character is literal.
